annotations.description: Mulliganed a functional 7-card hand with 4 lands, a turn-1 play (Swarm Shambler), a solid 3-drop (Crawling Sensation), and removal (Hunter's Edge). This hand has a reasonable curve and mana base for a green-based deck.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to mulligan down to 6 cards
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. It has adequate mana, a turn-1 play, and reasonable spells on curve. Going to 6 risks getting a worse hand with no guaranteed improvement.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a functional 7-card hand. While the hand had no green source (making Servant of the Scale uncastable), the remaining 6 cards formed an excellent blue curve: Warden of Evos Isle turn 3, Mistral Singer turn 3, Roaming Ghostlight turn 4 (discounted by Warden), with Rookie Mistake as protection. Two lands is acceptable with this curve, and the probability of drawing a third land by turn 3 is high (~75%+).
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. The blue core (Warden, Mistral Singer, Ghostlight, Rookie Mistake) is strong enough to win without green mana, and going to 6 risks getting a worse hand while losing a card.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a 6-card hand with one land (Plains) down to 5 cards. While the hand was land-light with only one Plains and mostly green spells, one-land keeps on 6 are common in Limited since going to 5 is so punishing. The hand had a good curve (2-drops through 5-drop) and could function if even one or two lands were drawn in the first couple turns.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 6-card hand. While risky with one land, the curve is solid and a 5-card hand is extremely disadvantaged. Drawing even one Forest makes multiple cards castable.

annotations.description: Mulliganed a keepable 6-card hand down to 5. The hand had 2 Forests, Benevolent Hydra (castable turn 2-3 with just green), Hunter's Edge (castable turn 4 with just green), and two blue cards that come online with any Island draw. While not perfect, this hand has lands and a functional green curve. Going to 5 cards is a significant card disadvantage that risks getting a worse hand.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 6-card hand. It has 2 lands, castable green spells (Benevolent Hydra and Hunter's Edge), and upside if any blue source is drawn. A 5-card hand is statistically likely to be worse.

annotations.description: Bouncing the summoning-sick Moldgraf Millipede with Unsubstantiate is a tempo-negative play. The Millipede will return and mill 3 more cards, likely growing even larger (4 creatures already in opponent's graveyard). This wastes Unsubstantiate as a temporary answer that makes the problem worse. Meanwhile, the opponent can't attack with the Millipede this turn anyway since it's summoning sick.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Unsubstantiate to bounce the summoning-sick 5/5 Moldgraf Millipede
annotations.betterLine: Cast Hydra's Growth on Servant of the Scale. The Millipede is summoning sick so there's no immediate threat. Hydra's Growth creates an exponential clock (2/2 immediately, 4/4 next upkeep, 8/8 the turn after) that demands an answer, and Unsubstantiate is preserved for a more impactful moment like protecting the enchanted creature or bouncing a lethal attacker.

annotations.description: Cast Adventurous Impulse (which only finds a creature or land from top 3) instead of Scale the Heights, which would put a +1/+1 counter on Servant of the Scale, gain 2 life, grant an extra land drop, AND draw a card. Scale the Heights is strictly superior here - it advances the board, gains life against a threatening 7/7 Millipede, and the card draw + extra land drop helps reach 4 mana for Capture Sphere next turn to answer the Millipede.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Adventurous Impulse for G, leaving UU open with nothing to spend it on
annotations.betterLine: Cast Scale the Heights targeting Servant of the Scale, gaining 2 life, drawing a card, and getting an extra land drop to accelerate toward casting Capture Sphere (3U) next turn to neutralize the 7/7 Millipede

annotations.description: With only 2 lands in play and a 7/7 Moldgraf Millipede threatening to attack next turn, taking Domesticated Hydra (which costs 2GG and needs double green with only 1 Forest) over Island is questionable. The Island could be played immediately (land drop available) to reach 3 lands, accelerating toward Capture Sphere (3U) to neutralize the 7/7 threat. Domesticated Hydra is far from castable given the mana situation.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Domesticated Hydra from Adventurous Impulse
annotations.betterLine: Take Island to play it immediately, reaching 3 lands and getting closer to casting Capture Sphere (3U) next turn to handle the 7/7 Moldgraf Millipede. Scale the Heights in hand can also find more lands and draw cards.

annotations.description: GPT54 passed with the option to sacrifice Kami of Ancient Law to destroy Capture Sphere (which is likely locking down one of their creatures). While keeping the Kami as a 2/2 body has some value, destroying Capture Sphere to free a locked creature is likely worth more, especially since the Kami could be removed by the opponent before GPT54 gets another chance to use it.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, keeping Kami of Ancient Law on the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Kami of Ancient Law's sacrifice ability to destroy Capture Sphere, freeing the enchanted creature. The 2/2 body is less valuable than unlocking whatever creature Capture Sphere is tapping down.

annotations.description: Cast Soul's Might before Scale the Heights, missing the opportunity to first put a +1/+1 counter on Domesticated Hydra (making it 4/4) so Soul's Might next turn would yield 4 counters instead of 3. Also missed drawing a card, gaining 2 life, and using the extra land drop from Scale the Heights this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Soul's Might on Domesticated Hydra (3/3) for 3 +1/+1 counters, making it 6/6.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Grove (tapped), then cast Scale the Heights targeting Domesticated Hydra — gaining 2 life, drawing a card, getting a +1/+1 counter (Hydra becomes 4/4), and an extra land drop. Next turn, cast Soul's Might on the 4/4 Hydra for 4 counters (8/8 total), plus potentially play Hydra's Growth.

annotations.description: Declined to block a 6/6 trampling Hydra when Archon of Justice (4/4) was available to block. Blocking with Archon would save 4 life (take 2 trample instead of 6) AND trigger Archon's death ability to exile any permanent - most importantly the Domesticated Hydra itself, removing the opponent's biggest threat. Instead, GPT54 took 6 damage for free and kept an Archon that could have traded for enormous value.
annotations.actionTaken: No blocks declared, taking 6 damage from the trampling Hydra.
annotations.betterLine: Block with Archon of Justice. Take only 2 trample damage, Archon dies and its trigger exiles the Domesticated Hydra (or Capture Sphere to free the Hornbeetle). This saves 4 life and removes the opponent's primary threat.

annotations.description: The player declined to sacrifice Kami of Ancient Law to destroy the Capture Sphere that is locking down their 7/7 Moldgraf Millipede. With both players at 13 life, freeing a 7/7 creature is vastly more impactful than keeping a 2/2 body. The player already has Archon of Justice (4/4 flying), Iridescent Hornbeetle (3/4), and Skyhunter Patrol (though summoning sick) as other threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Kami of Ancient Law's sacrifice ability to destroy Capture Sphere.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Kami of Ancient Law to destroy Capture Sphere, freeing the 7/7 Moldgraf Millipede for combat. Trading a 2/2 to unlock a 7/7 is excellent value, especially with the opponent at 13 life and vulnerable to a massive attack.

annotations.description: Bounced Archon of Justice (4/4 flyer) instead of Moldgraf Millipede (7/7). The Millipede is the largest stat threat and bouncing it uniquely resets its +1/+1 counters (it re-enters as 2/2 and regrows from graveyard count, likely reaching ~5/5 instead of 7/7). The Archon comes back at full 4/4 when recast. Both cost 5 mana to replay, but resetting the Millipede's counters provides a more permanent advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Archon of Justice with Roaming Ghostlight's bounce
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Moldgraf Millipede to reset its 5 +1/+1 counters, significantly reducing the biggest threat on the board from 7/7 to likely ~4-5/4-5 when recast

annotations.description: Blocked Skyhunter Patrol (2/3 with flying and first strike) with Roaming Ghostlight (3/2 flying). First strike means Skyhunter deals 2 damage to Ghostlight, killing it before Ghostlight can deal any damage back. Ghostlight dies for nothing - no trade occurs.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Skyhunter Patrol with Roaming Ghostlight, losing the Ghostlight to first strike without killing the Skyhunter.
annotations.betterLine: Either block Kami of Ancient Law (2/2) to trade evenly, or don't block at all to preserve the 3/2 flyer for future attacks (taking 7 going to 6 life, but keeping a flying threat against opponent at 7 life). Not blocking preserves the ability to counter-attack with Ghostlight + Hydra for potential lethal next turn.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 7 life with zero untapped creatures that can block (all are either tapped or have summoning sickness). Domesticated Hydra is 7/7 - exactly lethal. Opponent has only 2 untapped lands (Forest + Plains) and 1 card in hand, which is insufficient mana for any common removal spell that could stop this attack (Divine Verdict costs 4, etc.).
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack, passing the combat phase with no attackers declared.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Domesticated Hydra 7/7 for exactly lethal damage (7 damage to a 7-life opponent with no available blockers).
